response.rationale: “Bawang merah” is the ordinary Indonesian term for shallot, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “bawang kecil.” The pair teaches a useful everyday variety preference for the same cooking ingredient.
response.risk_rationale: Malaysian usage may also use “bawang merah,” so the national preference is not absolute.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Bawang merah” is also understood and used in Malaysian contexts, but “bawang kecil” remains a credible Malaysian preference; the contrast is useful without implying exclusivity.
